root_motivation: Tool authors — today the fleet's own adapters, tomorrow any agent publishing a tool that talks to a configurable upstream — cannot pass a non-secret value into their tool's runtime. The evidence is a shipped workaround: PRD-fleet-adapter-secret-env-fallback (queued 2026-09-12) exists solely because the adapter's plain settings had no path into the sandbox except the secret store, and the dream note that drafted it recorded "product component noted, not drafted: mcphost-python-kind-plain-env" (dream-log 2026-09-12T18:00Z). The misuse has real costs: secrets are AES-encrypted rows with a rotation story, `tool_test` redacts them by design, and an operator auditing the secret store cannot tell credentials from configuration — so the one store whose hygiene matters most fills with values that were never secret. The production tools table already shows authors improvising around missing configuration: seven live tools carry a literal `{{workspace_host}}` placeholder in their URL tem...
user_persona: An agent (real or the demand-fleet harness) calling signup for the first time, whose whole session -- including any client-side transcript its own harness keeps -- must not leak a live, indefinitely-usable credential; secondarily the operator (Joe) who pulled this forward on 2026-09-12 with 'test it' once a real tenant's exposure story was on the line, and who reads host.key_rotate's audit trail (journal, never secret values) after a suspected leak.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a python publish with `env: {"UPSTREAM_URL": "https://example.test"}`, When the tool is called, Then the process observes `UPSTREAM_URL` with that value and the call succeeds.
Given env names `MCPHOST_X`, `PATH`, and `lower_case`, When each is published, Then each publish is refused with a structured error naming the key and the violated rule.

Given an env map with 17 entries, and another totaling over 4 KiB, When published, Then each is refused with a structured error naming the bound; Given exactly 16 entries under 4 KiB, Then publish succeeds.

Given a tool with secret `API_KEY` set, When a publish declares env `API_KEY`, Then it is refused naming the collision; Given a tool published with env `MODE`, When `secret_set MODE` is attempted, Then it is refused symmetrically.
Given a tool with secret `API_KEY` and env `MODE=fast`, When `host.tool_test` runs, Then the rendered environment shows `MODE=fast` verbatim, `API_KEY` redacted, and each labeled as env or secret.

Given a tool with env and no secrets, When called under the sandbox, Then the values are present and the sandbox profile is byte-identical to the secrets-only case apart from the variables themselves.

Given the descriptor and llms.txt after build, When grepped, Then `env` is documented with its bounds and the env-versus-secret distinction, and `host.tool_get` returns the env map for a tool that has one.

Given a published tool with a warm pooled process, When its env map is updated without source changes, Then the next call observes the new values (the pooled process was invalidated) and no republish of source occurred.
Given a publish with env, When the journal/audit row is read, Then it records the env names and never the values.
Given an admin inspection of a tool with env, When invoked, Then it reports env names and total size, never values.

scope: signup gains an opt-in `handoff` boolean argument (default false/unchanged): true returns {tenant, tenant_id, handoff_token, expires_in, usage, next} with no `key` field at all, instead of today's {tenant, key, namespace, endpoint, usage, next} (P0, AC1).

New unauthenticated `host.redeem(handoff_token)` exchanges a valid, unexpired, not-yet-redeemed token for the tenant key exactly once via an atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE redeemed_unix IS NULL` claim; a second redemption fails `handoff_token_redeemed`, an expired one fails `handoff_token_expired`, neither ever echoing the token (P0, AC2, AC6).

New authenticated `host.key_rotate` (current key or tenant_key argument) issues a new key, overwrites `tenants.key_hash` and stamps `key_rotated_unix` in one statement, so the presented key stops resolving via `find_tenant_by_key_hash` from that call onward (P0, AC3).

Storage: migration 0019 adds `handoff_tokens` (token stored hashed via the existing `hash_key` convention; the raw key is AES-256-GCM-encrypted with the same `AppState::secrets::SecretBox` `host.secret_set` already uses, decrypted exactly once at redemption) and `tenants.key_rotated_unix` (P0, AC4/AC6).
`host.whoami` gains `key_age_s`/`key_rotated_at`, derived from `key_rotated_unix` falling back to `created_unix` for a never-rotated key (P1, AC8).

Docs: `get_info`'s instructions, `host.quickstart`'s unauthenticated step, README.md/docs/agent-quickstart.md/www/llms.txt (synced via scripts/gen-agent-docs.sh) all recommend the handoff flow while stating the raw path stays fully supported (P0, AC7).

A handoff_ac01-08 integration-test suite, including the full two-context replay test (AC4: signup handoff, redeem, rotate, replay the dead token, replay the dead key, confirm the live key works) Joe's 'test it' asked for.
non_goals: No OAuth and no session binding -- cycle 11's stateless-transport ruling (`with_legacy_session_mode(false)`) stands; handoff+redeem happens inside the same session the token narrows the exposure window on, it does not eliminate the key-as-argument constraint.
No forced migration of existing tenants or the harness -- the raw-key path (signup without `handoff`) is byte-identical to before (AC5) and stays the default; rotation is available, never mandatory.
No change to admin auth, `admin.*` tools, or the admin key's own resolution path.

No corpus-task/harness-probe wiring for AC9 (P1) in this build -- deferred, see PRD frontmatter `deferred_acs: [9]` / `mock_justifications`; it needs the demand-fleet's own synthorg harness, a different subsystem than mcphost.

additional.raw_path_byte_compatible: signup without the `handoff` argument (or with `handoff: false`) must return exactly today's {tenant, key, namespace, endpoint, usage, next} field set with no `handoff_token` key -- verified by tests/handoff_ac05_raw_signup_still_works_unchanged.rs's field-set equality assertion and its 17-tool-unaffected spirit (a representative subset actually called; PRD AC5).
additional.no_plaintext_secret_at_rest_or_in_output: the handoff token is stored only hashed (`hash_key`, the same convention `tenants.key_hash` already uses); the raw tenant key a handoff token stands in for is stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted via the existing `AppState::secrets::SecretBox` (the same cipher `host.secret_set` uses for tenant secrets), decrypted exactly once inside `control::redeem`; no `tracing::*!` call in `control::redeem`/`control::key_rotate` is ever passed a token or key value, only the handoff token row's own integer id (PRD AC6).
additional.single_use_atomic_claim: `Db::redeem_handoff_token`'s claim is a second `UPDATE handoff_tokens SET redeemed_unix = ?1 WHERE token_hash = ?2 AND redeemed_unix IS NULL` statement (not folded into the initial SELECT's decision), so two concurrent redemptions of the same token cannot both succeed -- the loser reads `AlreadyRedeemed` the same as a genuine later redemption would (PRD AC2).
additional.rotation_no_extra_query_per_call: `resolve_auth`/`resolve_tenant_key_auth`'s hot path is unchanged by rotation -- `Db::rotate_tenant_key` replaces `tenants.key_hash` in place in one UPDATE, so an old key simply stops matching the existing `find_tenant_by_key_hash` lookup; no new query was added per call (PRD Technical considerations).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a tenant key need anything beyond today's raw signup response?
five_whys_trace.a: Every tenant key issued passes through a model's context (as the `tenant_key` tools/call argument on all 17 tenant tools) and, for harness sessions, into recorded transcripts on disk -- 42 recordings retained from one run alone (vision 2026-09-09).

five_whys_trace.q: Why was this not fixed when the key-as-argument design was chosen (cycle 11)?
five_whys_trace.a: Cycle 11 accepted the exposure deliberately given the architectural constraints (one stateless connection, static headers, no session binding) and recorded a single-use handoff token as deferred rather than dismissed, with 'before the endpoint carries a real tenant' as the stated due date.

five_whys_trace.q: Why fix it now rather than wait for that due date?
five_whys_trace.a: Joe pulled it forward on 2026-09-12 with an explicit instruction to test it -- every tenant today is synthetic, which is exactly the window in which to prove the new path end-to-end before the first real agent signs up and its credential's exposure story is set.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a token-plus-redeem-plus-rotate shape rather than, say, short-lived keys or forced rotation?
five_whys_trace.a: The constraint set that forced key-as-argument in the first place (stateless transport, no session binding) still holds, so any fix has to work inside one session with no reconnect -- a single-use handoff token narrows the transcript's exposure window to the signup+redeem exchange, and on-demand rotation (not forced, since existing tenants/the harness must keep working unchanged) closes the window on suspicion of leak without a support ticket.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is this exposure reduction rather than elimination, and is that acceptable?
five_whys_trace.a: The key still has to reach the tenant as a `tools/call` argument eventually (same architectural constraint), so a transcript that captures the *redeem* response still captures a live key until the next rotation -- the PRD's own Technical considerations say this plainly rather than overclaiming elimination; AC4's replay test proves the *token* and any *rotated-out* key are dead, which is the actual, honest claim being made.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 9 offers two ways to fix the middleware doc/scope mismatch: re-scope the layer to /mcp, or correct the comment to say it is router-wide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
